memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If a man seduces a virgin who is not pledged to be married and sleeps with her, he must pay the bride-price, and she shall be his wife. If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, he must still pay the bride-price for virgins." - Exodus 22:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In a culture very different from ours, this law protected a young woman whose future could be devastated by a man who used her and moved on. God would not allow her to be treated as disposable. The man was held responsible — bound to provide, to commit, or to pay what was owed. Her dignity and her future were not his to toss aside. Even in a fallen world, God was guarding the vulnerable and taking intimacy seriously.

Beneath the ancient customs lies a timeless truth: sexual intimacy is not a casual thing to God. It carries weight, consequence, and the potential for both great blessing and great harm. Our culture often treats it as entertainment with no strings attached, but God has always known better. He designed intimacy for the safety and covenant of marriage, precisely because He cares about the hearts and futures of the people involved.

This is not old-fashioned prudishness; it is love. God's boundaries around intimacy exist to protect us, not to rob us of joy. The New Testament calls us to honour our bodies and one another, fleeing what harms and pursuing what is pure (1 Cor 6:18-20). Whatever your past, God's grace covers it fully, and His call forward is always toward wholeness, dignity, and love that keeps its promises.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I view God's boundaries around intimacy as protection or as restriction?
How can I honour the dignity of others rather than using people?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your boundaries flow from love, not harshness. Help me honour intimacy as You designed it and treat others with dignity, never as disposable. Amen.
